text.p: Equitable Resources Inc said Monday its natural gas and oil reserves increased to 850 billion cubic feet and 19.5 million barrels, respectively, at year end from 845 billion cubic feet and 18.2 million barrels a year earlier.

The company said its exploration and production unit replaced 119 percent of 1996 production of 67.7 billion cubic feet equivalent through extensions and discoveries, including two in the Gulf of Mexico announced Monday.

The first was on West Cameron Block 17, where the discovery well flowed 18 million cubic feet of natural gas and 121 barrels of condensate per day on a 29/64 inch choke at a pressure of 4,689 pounds per square flow through pipe at 14,130 feet. The well was drilled on a State of Louisiana lease acquired from Chevron Corp.
Equitable said it holds 66 percent working interest before reversionary farm-out interest and the other owners are individuals or private companies.

The second discovery, on Chandeleur Block 21, a federal lease, flowed 9.1 million cubic feet of natural gas on a 40/64 inch choke at a pressure of 1,250 pounds per square inch flow through pipe at about 6,112 feet. Equitable said it holds 40 percent working interest in this property where a production facility and pipeline have been installed.
"We are expanding our drilling and farm-in programs in the Gulf during 1997," Equitable concluded without specifics.
